---
title: "Direct estimation"
subtitle: "Survey design-based estimates and uncertainty"
---

```{r}
#| label: direct-setup
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(stringr)
library(tidyr)
library(sf)
library(ggplot2)
library(patchwork)
library(survey)
library(tibble)
library(scales)

base_path <- here::here("data")
output_path <- here::here("outputs")
dir.create(output_path, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

msoa_boundaries <- st_read(
  file.path(base_path, "boundaries-msoa.geojson"),
  quiet = TRUE
) |>
  rename(area_id = MSOA21CD) |>
  filter(str_starts(area_id, "W")) |>
  arrange(area_id)

domain_frame <- read_csv(
  file.path(base_path, "clean", "domain_msoayear.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| label: direct-plot-config
#| echo: false
share_label <- label_percent(accuracy = 1)
variance_label <- label_number(accuracy = 0.001)
missing_fill <- "grey85"

map_text_theme <- theme(
  plot.title.position = "plot",
  plot.title = element_text(size = 12, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30"),
  axis.title.y = element_text(
    size = 12,
    face = "bold",
    angle = 90,
    margin = margin(r = 15)
  ),
  legend.title = element_text(size = 10),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 9)
)

map_annotation_theme <- theme(
  plot.title.position = "plot",
  plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 15, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30")
)

chart_text_theme <- theme(
  plot.title.position = "plot",
  plot.title = element_text(size = 18, face = "bold", hjust = 0.5),
  plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 12, hjust = 0.5, colour = "grey30"),
  axis.title = element_text(size = 14),
  axis.text = element_text(size = 12),
  legend.text = element_text(size = 12)
)
```

## Estimation approach {.unnumbered}

{{< include assets/target-estimand.qmd >}}

Direct estimation is the starting point for the SAE workflow. Each area-time estimate, or *MSOA-year cell* in this example, is calculated only from the survey respondents observed in that area and wave. For each *MSOA-year cell*, we calculate a Horvitz--Thompson weighted proportion using the respondent cycling outcome, matched survey weight, survey stratum, MSOA assignment, and wave year.

The output is a transparent survey-based baseline: a direct estimate, sampling variance, and usable sample size for each observed *MSOA-year cell*. These estimates show where the survey evidence is strong, sparse, missing, or unstable, helping us decide whether model-based small area estimation is needed.

## Prepare survey data

We use a Horvitz–Thompson weighted proportion among usable adult respondents. The cleaned survey microdata input has one row per respondent-wave for the cycling estimand. After filtering, each retained row has a valid binary cycling response, matched weight, MSOA assignment, wave label, and survey stratum:

| Column | Role |
|---|---|
| `area_id` | Estimation area |
| `time_id` | Survey wave / year |
| `freq_cyclist` | Binary response:<br>`1` if the adult cycles for transport frequently,<br>`0` otherwise |
| `weight` | Matched weight |
| `strata` | Local Authority code |
```{r}
#| label: direct-load

survey_bike <- read_csv(
  file.path(base_path, "clean", "surveyind_freqcyc.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
) |>
  drop_na(freq_cyclist, weight, area_id, strata)

head(survey_bike)
```

## Calculate direct estimates

`svyby()` computes the weighted share and uncertainty diagnostics for every area-time cell with usable observations. The completed area-by-time grid retains missing cells for later modelling.

```{r}
#| label: direct-estimate
#| code-fold: false

# Define survey design
bike_design <- svydesign(
  ids = ~1,
  strata = ~strata,
  weights = ~weight,
  data = survey_bike
)

# Calculate direct estimate and uncertainty
direct_bike_estimates <- svyby(
  formula = ~freq_cyclist,
  by = ~area_id + time_id,
  design = bike_design,
  FUN = svymean,
  vartype = "se",
  na.rm = TRUE,
  keep.names = FALSE
) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  transmute(
    area_id,
    time_id,
    direct_estimate = freq_cyclist,
    variance = se^2
  )

# Calculate sample size per area-time cell
direct_bike_counts <- survey_bike |>
  group_by(area_id, time_id) |>
  summarise(n = n(), .groups = "drop")

# Join together
direct_bike <- domain_frame |>
  left_join(direct_bike_estimates, by = c("area_id", "time_id")) |>
  left_join(direct_bike_counts, by = c("area_id", "time_id")) |>
  mutate(n = replace_na(n, 0L))

head(direct_bike)
```

## Assess precision and coverage

Direct estimation provides a useful starting point because it makes three limitations visible:

- **Uneven coverage:** The number of usable observations varies across survey waves and MSOAs, leaving some area-time cells with much less direct evidence than others.
- **Unstable area estimates over time:** For some MSOAs, direct estimates change sharply between waves, which may reflect real change or simply sampling noise.
- **Invalid variances:** Since `freq_cyclist` is a binary indicator, all respondents in an area with a small sample size may give the same response. The estimated sampling variance is then zero, incorrectly suggesting that the prevalence estimate has no uncertainty. For all intents and purposes, these small-area estimates are unusable for further analysis.

```{r}
#| label: direct-map
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 16
#| fig-height: 12
#| out-width: "100%"
#| fig-align: "center"

# Plotting functions
base_map <- function(wave) {
  wave_direct <- direct_bike[direct_bike[["time_id"]] == wave, ]

  wave_data <- msoa_boundaries |>
    left_join(wave_direct, by = "area_id")

  ggplot(wave_data) +
    theme_void() +
    map_text_theme
}

plot_estimate <- function(wave) {
  base_map(wave) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(
        fill = if_else(
          is.na(direct_estimate) | direct_estimate == 0,
          NA_real_,
          direct_estimate
        )
      ),
      colour = "transparent"
    ) +
    scale_fill_viridis_c(
      option = "magma",
      limits = c(0, 1),
      labels = share_label,
      na.value = missing_fill,
      name = "Share"
    )
}

plot_uncertainty <- function(wave) {
  base_map(wave) +
    geom_sf(
      aes(fill = if_else(is.na(variance) | variance == 0, NA_real_, variance)),
      colour = "transparent"
    ) +
    scale_fill_distiller(
      palette = "Oranges",
      direction = 1,
      na.value = missing_fill,
      limits = c(0, max(direct_bike$variance, na.rm = TRUE)),
      labels = variance_label,
      name = "Variance"
    )
}

# Generate and assemble plots
e_21 <- plot_estimate("2021") +
  ggtitle("2021") +
  ylab("Direct estimate") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
e_23 <- plot_estimate("2023") +
  ggtitle("2023") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
e_25 <- plot_estimate("2025") + ggtitle("2025")

u_21 <- plot_uncertainty("2021") +
  ylab("Variance") +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
u_23 <- plot_uncertainty("2023") + theme(legend.position = "none")
u_25 <- plot_uncertainty("2025")

diagnostic_panel <- wrap_plots(
  e_21, e_23, e_25,
  u_21, u_23, u_25,
  ncol = 3, nrow = 2
) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Share of adults who cycle for transport frequently",
    subtitle = "Domains with invalid/missing estimates or sampling variances in grey",
    theme = map_annotation_theme
  )

direct_summary_by_wave <- direct_bike |>
  group_by(time_id) |>
  summarise(
    `Usable observations` = sum(n),
    `Median sample size` = median(n),
    `MSOAs without direct estimates` = sum(is.na(direct_estimate)),
    `MSOAs without variance` = sum(is.na(variance)),
    `MSOAs with invalid estimates` = sum(variance == 0, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  rename(Wave = time_id)

diagnostic_panel
direct_summary_by_wave
```

Sparse and uneven survey coverage at the target MSOA-year scale limits how far direct estimates can be reported on their own. This motivates the use of model-based SAE methods that borrow strength across areas, years, and auxiliary predictors to produce more stable estimates with appropriately quantified uncertainty.

Two model-based options follow:

- **Area-level SAE** stabilises direct MSOA-year estimates using sampling variances to control how much weight each direct estimate receives (Fay--Herriot model).
- **Unit-level SAE** estimates the individual outcome from survey microdata and aggregates predictions to target MSOA-years.

The choice between area-level and unit-level modelling should depend on the quality of the direct estimates and sampling variances as model inputs, and whether the survey microdata contain unit-level predictors that explain variation in the `freq_cyclist` binary indicator. 

In this example, the summary points to important limitations for area-level modelling since there are many domains with invalid variances. Nonetheless, we still fit an [area-level model](area-sae-fh.qmd) at the next workbook first to show how much stabilisation is possible from direct-estimate inputs before moving to [unit-level modelling](unit-sae-summ.qmd).

```{r}
#| label: direct-export
#| include: false
write_csv(direct_bike, file.path(output_path, "freqcyc_estimates_direct.csv"))
```
